Runnable examples

Scripting and a single-player gameKit multiplayerReplay simulation and networkingScrapyard: follow a complete feature

Choose the smallest example that demonstrates the behavior you want to change. The repository keeps Kit games and Replay games as independent projects. Run commands from the repository root with its development environment available.

Scripting and a single-player game#

Example What to inspect
Showcase setup A small scene using the script binding and typed engine calls
Survivors A top-down game with movement, enemies, effects, and authored scenes

Build a project with build/build_scripts.sh, then launch it with the Godot executable selected by the development shell:

Shell
nix develop
bash build/build_scripts.sh examples/survivors
"$GODOT" --path examples/survivors

Kit multiplayer#

Example What it demonstrates
Hello Net The smallest two-peer game with owner motion and shared entity state
Hello Sim The same square with server-authoritative fixed ticks and local prediction
Cavecrawl Interactions, inventory, AI, session identity, and recovery
Quickdraw Competitive rules, prediction, and historical hit queries
Claimball A contested ball with local presentation claims

Start with Hello Net and Hello Sim side by side. Keep an injected-delay run in the development loop so current-input prediction and watched presentation remain observable while gameplay changes.

Replay simulation and networking#

Example What it demonstrates
Loot Complete-world restoration and an independent reference comparison, without Godot
Session starter A small authored Godot project with direct offline and native network roles
Hello and Loot views Input capture, detached presentation, occurrence reconciliation, and lower-level network integration
Checked recipes Public lifecycle calls for Session, Party → Room, and admitted P2P setup
Duel Deterministic fixed-roster peer rollback

The examples have different network policies. Use their own README commands and test scope rather than inferring that one scene enables every runner feature.

Scrapyard: follow a complete feature#

Play the live browser build to try the game. The repository's Replay Scrapyard guide then follows a shared turret through authored definitions, input, simulation, and scene composition. Its workbenches provide isolated actor and HUD previews as well as encounters that run the actual gameplay rules.

Use the code guide to find an input handler, frame service, simulation rule, or view. Use the feature guide's focused tests before running a full multiplayer scenario.
